overview.summary: Dentists diagnose, treat and prevent problems of the teeth, gums and mouth, and advise people how to keep them healthy.
overview.problems: They relieve pain, repair damaged teeth, treat gum disease and help people avoid decay.
overview.worksWith: Patients of all ages, dental nurses, hygienists, dental technicians and other health professionals.
overview.workplaces: Dental clinics, hospitals, community health services and private practice, and some dentists run their own practices.

timeline.title: Prepare for patients
timeline.description: The dentist reviews the day's appointments and notes and checks that equipment is clean and ready.
timeline.why: Preparation and infection control protect patients.

timeline.title: Check-ups and treatments
timeline.description: The dentist examines teeth and gums, takes and reads X-rays, removes decay, fills teeth and explains what is found.
timeline.why: Finding problems early makes treatment simpler.

timeline.title: Records and planning
timeline.description: The dentist writes notes, plans longer treatments such as crowns or braces and contacts specialists.
timeline.why: Clear plans help patients understand cost and time.

timeline.title: More patients and procedures
timeline.description: The dentist carries out extractions, root canal treatment or other procedures, using anaesthetic to keep patients comfortable.
timeline.why: Skilled, calm work reduces fear and pain.

timeline.title: Team debrief and admin
timeline.description: The dentist talks over the day with dental nurses and handles supplies and bookings.
timeline.why: A well-run team keeps patients safe and appointments on time.

timeline.title: Emergencies and anxious patients
timeline.description: Some patients arrive in pain or are very nervous.
timeline.why: Patients who feel safe are more likely to seek care early.

responsibilities: Treating decay, gum disease and injuries
Giving local anaesthetic and managing pain
Advising on prevention, such as brushing and diet
challenges: The work is very precise and done in a small space, which can strain the neck and back.
Some patients are nervous or in pain.
A full appointment book creates time pressure.
Running a practice involves business, staff and equipment costs.
workEnvironment: Clean, well-lit treatment rooms in clinics, hospitals or community services, with a team that includes dental nurses. The work is seated or standing close to patients. Hours are often regular, and some dentists work evenings or Saturdays.
rewards: Relieving pain and improving smiles and confidence
A mix of science, craft and people skills
The option to run your own practice
tradeoffs: Income and conditions that vary by country and type of practice

activity.title: Create a one-page guide to healthy teeth
steps: Read about tooth decay and gum health on a trusted source such as your national dental association or health service.
Write the three most useful habits for healthy teeth and why each works.
Explain them aloud to a family member in simple words.
Ask whether anything was unclear and improve the guide.
Note whether explaining health to others felt rewarding.
activity.outcome: You practise turning health information into clear advice, which dentists give every day.
activity.safety: This is an information exercise only. Do not examine or treat anyone's teeth, and see a dentist for real dental problems.

source: Written by Futurixia from general knowledge of how this profession works. It is illustrative and is not based on interviews or surveys.
